content.thinking:
I'm setting up the JSON spec now, with the decision order fixed as decline, escalate, request_docs, incomplete, approve under SOP 2.1. For the unknowns handling, I'll use the rule from SOP 2.2: if any required fact is unknown, the case can't be approved, and it falls under "incomplete."

I'm checking whether an approve rule is needed, since the order includes approve and the first matching outcome wins. I'm weighing a rule that applies when nothing else does, quoting the section 1 wording that all requirements are met and no risk factor applies.

I'm settling how the collections rule should count people: the SOP ties the identified individuals to the control person and to every owner at 25% or more, and I'm wondering whether the excluded-entity and nonprofit cases change which of those applies.

I'm now weighing how the collections rule should count people. The SOP's "identified individuals" means the control person and owners at 25% or more, but the nonprofit and excluded-entity exceptions might drop the owner part, and I need to decide whether the agent's own listings count.

I'm working out whether certification changes the owner count: the SOP never mentions it, so I'll use share_pct as written. For excluded entities no beneficial owners are required, so the identified-individuals rule should only pick up the control person and 25%+ owners when the entity isn't excluded, and nonprofits still get a control person.

I'm settling the counts_when text now: the SOP's identify-every-25%-owner sentence sits in section 3.3, but the control person comes from 3.2, and each cited section has to contain its quoted text, so I need to pick one.

I'm settling on the counts_when text now, and I'm leaning toward citing section 3.3 for the 25%-owner rule, since its exact sentence is there. The control person comes from 3.2, but I can only quote one section, so I'll note the 3.2 wording in the sections list.

I'm looking at how the empty-OK rule should apply: the excluded case is covered by the 25%-owner sentence in section 3.3, so I'll let that sentence carry the exception, though I still need to check whether a non-excluded entity with no identified individuals should ever count as empty-OK.

I'm working out how the unaccounted-share check interacts with the excluded-entity exception, since an excluded owner's share shouldn't push the ownership-completeness flag.

I'm working out how an excluded entity's smaller shares should count: an excluded holder below 25% could still sit in front of an individual who reaches 25% combined with unaccounted shares, so those amounts need to go into the ownership-completeness sum, which means using "not at_least 25" since there's no less-than condition.

I'm now checking whether a person with a known share below 25% could still reach 25% once the unaccounted shares are added, since the SOP's completeness test is about unidentified people and not only the unaccounted total.

I'm checking whether a person who isn't counted, with a known share under 25%, could still reach 25% once the unaccounted shares are added to them. The problem is that a `some` condition only looks at people where counts_when holds, so that check can't see unidentified owners and I'll need another way to express it.

I'm checking whether a known share below 25% could still reach 25% once the unaccounted shares are added to it, but the `some` condition only looks at identified people, so that combined case can't be expressed there. I'll rely on the unaccounted-share total for the completeness test and leave the combined known-share case aside for now.

I'm asking whether a person not identified could reach 25% by adding the open share to their known share, but the `some` condition can't see people outside the identified set, so I'll note it under needs and leave the case-by-case check to the reviewer.

I'm checking the control-person condition next, since SOP 3.2 says that if no control person is identified, the case needs documents. Listing matters less than the screening itself: a known owner at 25% or more still counts as identified, and if their screening facts are missing the case is incomplete.

I'm looking at whether an over-allocated cap table, where the listed shares add up to more than 100%, needs its own handling, since the SOP doesn't address it directly and I still have to decide whether the spec should treat it as a separate outcome.

I'm checking whether over-allocated cap tables need separate handling in the 3.3 rule, since the SOP doesn't address them. I'll leave that out of the spec and keep the unaccounted-share test as written.

I'm checking the completeness wording again: ownership counts as complete only when no unidentified person could reach 25%, and an excluded entity's share at or above 25% needs no individual named. I'll take the open-share total as the test and leave the case of a known holder whose share plus the unaccounted shares reaches 25% for the reviewer.

I'm checking the sanctions rule in section 4.1, which fires if any entity or identified person has a confirmed sanctions match, and I'm also looking at the 3.4 identity check and the 3.5 registry-age test, which applies even to excluded entities.

I'm checking the sanctions rules now: a confirmed match on the entity or any identified person means decline, and a potential match that hasn't been cleared means escalate. I'm also noting that the adverse-media rule depends on a materiality bar I'll have to take as a given fact, and that the record-keeping requirement has no outcome attached to it.

I'm settling the adverse-media rule now: escalate if it's on the entity or any identified person, but only when the coverage is material and the report meets the SOP's match standard. The search record requirement has no outcome attached, so I'll list it under needs. Next I'm mapping the prohibited industries in section 5.1 to decline.

I'm checking whether an ordinary industry with no word in the SOP's prohibited list would be treated as unknown, which would leave every normal business incomplete, so I'll need to decide how to handle words that aren't in any mapping.

I'm settling the industry mapping now: the SOP lists prohibited industries that should decline and money services businesses and virtual currency that escalate, but it never says which industries are unrestricted, so I'll flag that gap in the needs list rather than guess at ordinary business words.

I'm weighing how the industry mapping should treat licensed money services businesses, since the SOP has 5.2 escalating them but 5.3 allowing approval once a state licence is verified. I'm checking how to express that without one rule overriding the other.

I'm weighing whether the 5.3 approval for licensed money services businesses can sit alongside the 5.2 escalation, since the two rules point in opposite directions for the same industry. An approve rule won't win against an escalate rule because escalate is more severe, so I'm considering whether to state the rules as written and let the contradiction show, rather than repairing it by adding a licence condition to 5.2.

I'm weighing whether the licensed-MSB approval in 5.3 can stand next to the 5.2 escalation, since as written an approve outcome loses to escalate and would never govern. The alternative reading is that 5.3 is an exception to 5.2 for msb cases with a verified licence, but I'm leaving the contradiction as the SOP states it rather than repairing it.

I'm weighing the 5.2 escalation against the 5.3 approval for verified licensed money services businesses, since as written the approval can never win over an escalation. I'll keep the two rules literal rather than adding a licence exception to 5.2, and flag the conflict. If the case is an MSB with an unknown licence status, the escalation still governs.

I'm working through the approve default and the unknowns handling, then mapping the sanctions rules: any sanctioned country on the entity or a person's residence leads to decline, and high-risk jurisdictions lead to escalate.

I'm settling the needs list now: the record-search requirement in 4.4 has no outcome attached, so it goes there, along with the unidentified-person case under 3.3 and the gap in the industry mapping, since the SOP names no industry that is neither prohibited nor restricted.

I'm settling the counts_when condition: a person counts when the entity isn't excluded and either the control person flag is yes or the nonprofit flag is no with share_pct at least 25. I'm also checking that an unknown excluded flag would still let the person count, which is acceptable here.

I'm settling the sanctions rule: the entity or any identified individual located in a comprehensively sanctioned country means decline, and I'm leaving the collection wording to section 3.3's first sentence, with the control person from 3.2 noted alongside it.

I'm drafting the approve rule from section 1, which requires that all requirements are met and no risk factor applies, and checking the exact wording against the source. Next I'm mapping industries: the prohibited ones (marijuana-related, adult content, unlicensed money transmission) to prohibited, money services businesses to msb, and virtual currency to crypto, with licensed money services businesses also mapped to msb.

I'm writing the sum over excluded owners and the 25% open-share test into the ownership rule, then describing the needs entry for people who aren't identified.

I'm noting that the ownership test has to catch a person who isn't identified and whose known share is under 25%, since the open share could push them over the line. The `some` condition can't reach people outside the counted set, and the format has no maximum, so for now I'm relying on the open-share total alone and leaving the per-person case as a needs item.

unknowns.text: If any fact required by this procedure is unknown, the case cannot be approved.

people.text: Unless the entity is excluded or is a nonprofit, identify every individual who owns 25% or more of the entity, directly or indirectly.

computed.text: If an excluded entity owns 25% or more, no individual needs to be identified for that share.

rules.text: all requirements below are met and no risk factor applies.

For every other entity, identify one control person: a single individual with significant responsibility to control, manage or direct the entity. If no control person is identified, request documents.

Unless the entity is excluded or is a nonprofit, identify every individual who owns 25% or more of the entity, directly or indirectly. Ownership is complete only when no unidentified person could own 25% or more, given the shares that are unaccounted for or held through entities whose owners are unknown. If an excluded entity owns 25% or more, no individual needs to be identified for that share. If ownership is not complete, request documents.
Verify the identity of every identified individual. If any is unverified, request documents.
The entity's registry filing must be less than 12 months old. Otherwise request documents.
A confirmed sanctions match on the entity or any identified individual: decline.
A potential sanctions match that has not been cleared: escalate.
A politically exposed person among the identified individuals: escalate.

Adverse media on the entity or any identified individual: escalate. Adverse media counts only if it is material. A report counts only if it matches the name and at least one other identifier (age, location or role), and comes from a court record, a regulator or an established news outlet, or from two independent other sources.
Prohibited industries (marijuana-related business, adult content, unlicensed money transmission): decline.
Restricted industries (money services businesses, virtual currency): escalate.
Licensed money services businesses whose state licence has been verified may be approved.
The entity or any identified individual is located in a comprehensively sanctioned country: decline.
The entity or any identified individual is located in a FATF high-risk or increased-monitoring jurisdiction: escalate.

sections.note: Defines the five outcomes. Approve is the default rule; the order in 2.1 lets any other rule that applies win over it.
Sets `order`: decline, escalate, request_docs, incomplete, approve.
Sets `unknowns`: a rule that might apply because of an unknown fact leads to incomplete. Section 1 defines Incomplete as a required fact not yet established.

Becomes the people list's `empty_ok_when` (excluded = yes) and `counts_when` (no identified individuals when excluded). It is also the excluded = no condition in control-person-missing and ownership-incomplete.
The control person is also part of the people list's `counts_when` (control_person = yes, unless excluded).

Also sets the people list's `counts_when` (owners of 25% or more, unless excluded or nonprofit). It also defines the computed `open_share_pct`: excluded-entity holdings under 25% stay open. 3.3 exempts only holdings of 25% or more. Over-allocation (`over_allocated`) is not mentioned anywhere in the SOP, so no rule uses it.
The SOP does not say whose potential match counts. The rule covers the entity and any identified individual, as 4.1 does.
The materiality bar is applied by the pack (`adverse_media` / `entity_adverse_media` mean media that meets it). The requirement to record searches has no outcome and no fact; see `needs`.

Translated as written. It conflicts with 5.2: a verified licensed MSB is still a money services business, which 5.2 escalates, and under 2.1 escalate outranks approve. So this rule can never decide a case. A person must decide whether 5.3 is meant as an exception to 5.2.

needs.text: Ownership is complete only when no unidentified person could own 25% or more, given the shares that are unaccounted for or held through entities whose owners are unknown.
needs.fact: Whether any person who is not an identified individual (a known owner under 25%) could reach 25% if the open share were theirs, i.e. share_pct + open_share_pct >= 25 for such a person. The people list's `counts_when` hides these people from `some`, and the format has no maximum. So the rule checks only the open share by itself (open_share_pct >= 25).

needs.text: Record every search: the terms, the date and the sources reviewed.
needs.fact: Whether the adverse media searches were recorded (terms, date, sources). No given fact says this, and the SOP gives no outcome when they are not recorded.

needs.text: Restricted industries (money services businesses, virtual currency): escalate.
needs.fact: Which case words mean an industry that is neither prohibited nor restricted (`normal`). The SOP names no such industry. Any industry word not in `maps.industry` is unknown, so an ordinary business can only reach approve if the case uses the word `normal`.
